title: Five metrics APIs, on round 8's real runs
brief: Five runnable APIs for the performance metrics per part type (Zach's note of 2026-11-17), each torchmetrics-shaped with numpy inside, math-only base metrics named by aliases, gates outside compute(), live = offline, and each one matching round 8's scorecard on 252 real plays.
defaultWhy: Folded values (v4) leads at 84 of 100. It is the only variant that meets the prior-art note's central recommendation (the state is a value: live is a fold, runs merge with no extra code), and its gates say what the scorecard's median hides: one alias, 'tip stop error', carries the median gate and Zach's 1 mm on every stop, judged into RobotDx's own Result, so CAN 11 fails 3 rungs on the every-stop objective and 99 % of its 84 stops reads 79 of 84. Closest: robot_metrics (v1) at 80, the literal torchmetrics port Zach liked; it loses points only where its state hides in attributes and its gates are plain thresholds.
decisionHinge: The lead rests on fr3 and fr4 (honest streaming and tail-aware gates). Weight 'reads like torchmetrics' instead (v1's add_state and Metric.plot()) or move 10 points to fr1 (the part's adjacency: v2 and v5 score 5 there with medium confidence) and v1 ties v4. Either way the splice keeps v4's value state and gates under v1's torchmetrics face; the open question is whether Zach wants update(state, chunk) visible or hidden behind Stream.
invariants: robot_msgs streams in; SI inside, degrees and mm shown
the generic rows are robot_msgs.compare's; the stop rule one shared per-sample kernel
one dataset: round 8's 252 real plays, the twin's 252 answers, the five-bar's 10 rungs
every variant passes the frozen parity check before it is scored
boundary: Prototypes in docs/proposals/metrics-api-2026-11-17/ that import robot_msgs and robot_models; nothing in src/, robot_msgs, sim2real, io-diagnostics, robotparts or bam_ws changed. W&B payloads are built, not sent; Rerun .rrd files are written locally.

variants.name: robot_metrics (torchmetrics, ported)
variants.thesis: A literal numpy port of torchmetrics: add_state states, update/compute/reset/merge_state, wrappers and compute groups, in its own robot_metrics package; a part type lists aliases as .metrics.
variants.bestWhen: You want torchmetrics' muscle memory exactly, and live monitors that run for hours (bounded state).
variants.losesWhen: State hides in attributes: merge needs each reduce rule right, compute() mid-run deep-copies the open tracker, and collections with different configs (stations' tip lengths) merge only through gates.
